questions.stem: A clinician presses on the swollen lower legs shown and the skin retains a lasting indentation. This physical finding is most characteristically associated with which category of disease?

explanation.summary: The lasting indentation identifies pitting edema, which reflects excess mobile interstitial fluid and is classically linked to cardiac, hepatic, or renal disease. Myxedema is nonpitting, angioedema and cellulitis are localized and acute, and lymphatic obstruction tends to produce nonpitting lymphedema.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lasting indentation identifies pitting edema, which reflects excess mobile interstitial fluid and is classically linked to cardiac, hepatic, or renal disease. Myxedema is nonpitting, angioedema and cellulitis are localized and acute, and lymphatic obstruction tends to produce nonpitting lymphedema.

questions.stem: The far-right branch of this classification of edema causes points to a protein-losing renal process. Which single laboratory abnormality would you most expect to underlie that branch?

explanation.summary: The protein-loss branch reflects nephrotic-range urinary albumin loss, which lowers serum albumin and thus plasma oncotic pressure, promoting fluid movement into the interstitium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The protein-loss branch reflects nephrotic-range urinary albumin loss, which lowers serum albumin and thus plasma oncotic pressure, promoting fluid movement into the interstitium.

questions.stem: In the capillary force diagram shown, which change to the depicted forces would MOST directly favor net filtration and lead to edema?

explanation.summary: A rise in capillary hydrostatic pressure pushes more fluid out of the capillary into the interstitium. Raising plasma oncotic pressure or albumin would pull fluid back in, reduced permeability limits leak, and higher interstitial hydrostatic pressure opposes filtration.
explanation.whyCorrect: A rise in capillary hydrostatic pressure pushes more fluid out of the capillary into the interstitium. Raising plasma oncotic pressure or albumin would pull fluid back in, reduced permeability limits leak, and higher interstitial hydrostatic pressure opposes filtration.

questions.stem: The green vessels emphasized in this illustration perform which function that is critical to preventing edema?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delivering oxygenated blood to the tissues

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exchanging gases across the capillary bed

explanation.summary: The green channels are lymphatic vessels, which collect the roughly 20 L/day of interstitial fluid not reabsorbed by venules and return it to the veins. Impairment of this drainage causes lymphedema.
explanation.whyCorrect: The green channels are lymphatic vessels, which collect the roughly 20 L/day of interstitial fluid not reabsorbed by venules and return it to the veins. Impairment of this drainage causes lymphedema.

questions.stem: In this summary diagram, the inflow branch grouping malabsorption, nephrotic syndrome, liver failure, and malnutrition acts through a fall in plasma oncotic pressure. Which underlying change best accounts for that branch?

explanation.summary: Albumin is the principal determinant of plasma oncotic pressure. Loss (nephrotic syndrome), decreased synthesis (liver failure, malnutrition), or poor intake/absorption lowers albumin, reducing the inward oncotic force and allowing fluid to accumulate in the interstitium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Albumin is the principal determinant of plasma oncotic pressure. Loss (nephrotic syndrome), decreased synthesis (liver failure, malnutrition), or poor intake/absorption lowers albumin, reducing the inward oncotic force and allowing fluid to accumulate in the interstitium.
